title: AITA for refusing to clean after my roommates' party?
text: I share an apartment with two friends. Last weekend, one roommate asked me to clean the entire kitchen after a party I did not attend. I explained that I had already cleaned my own dishes and had an important deadline the next morning. I offered to help organize a cleaning schedule, but they insisted that I do everything immediately. We argued in our group chat, and now they say I am selfish for refusing.

comments.text: You should not have to clean up their party.
Your roommates should take responsibility.
Everyone sharing the apartment should contribute.
Offering to create a schedule was reasonable.
You did not attend the party.

title: AITA for confronting my sister at dinner?
text: My sister and I planned a family dinner together. I booked the table after she said any restaurant would be fine. Later she complained that I chose a place she disliked and told relatives I had ignored her preferences. I pointed out her earlier message, but she said I should have asked again. During dinner I brought up the messages in front of everyone. She became upset and left early. We both think the other handled the situation badly.

comments.text: Bringing it up publicly was unnecessary.
She originally approved your decision.
Did she mention any dietary restrictions?
You followed the plan you agreed on.
You could have discussed it privately.
Both of you communicated poorly.

text: I was asked to take responsibility for supplies at a club event. The organizer told me to buy whatever was necessary, but did not give a budget or explain how reimbursement would work. I paid for several items and later requested repayment. The organizer said some purchases were unnecessary and refused to reimburse me. I do not know whether there was an approved spending limit, and I have not seen the rules that other volunteers were given.

comments.text: The organizer should explain the budget.
Was there a written spending policy?
You should have checked before buying.
The instruction was unclear.
Both sides should clarify expenses.
You acted on the organizer's request.

title: AITA for disagreeing with another volunteer?
text: Our volunteer team had to prepare a room for a community meeting. I arrived early and started arranging chairs according to the schedule we had received. Another volunteer wanted a different layout and asked me to redo everything. I said we should ask the organizer first, but they moved some chairs while I was working. Later I sent a message explaining what happened. The discussion became heated, and several people posted comments about who should apologize.

comments.text: You followed the original instructions.
Did the organizer approve the new layout?
You tried to clarify the plan.
